about: The same machine, stopped: `stop` runs a <cancel> of the send with the id `timer`, the five-second `timeout`, and removes only that one. The other three sends are still delivered, in the order of `static_timers`, and the machine never reaches `done` however long it waits. Every read is at least 500ms from a due time, so an engine on a real clock reads the same answer as one on a manual clock. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: armed on entering `waiting`; nothing has been delivered
`stop` cancels the send with the id `timer`; it changes no variable
2500ms in: `beat` then `echo`, due together, are still delivered in the order they were sent
5500ms in: past the five seconds `timeout` was due at, it was cancelled, so the machine is still waiting
